User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the WebStarter application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

email.description: The email address of the user.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the user account was last updated.

GeneratedComponent.title: GeneratedComponent
GeneratedComponent.description: Represents a UI Component or API Endpoint generated by the GenAI tool.

id.description: Unique identifier for the generated component entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who generated this component. (Relationship: User 1:N GeneratedComponent)

componentType.description: The type of the generated component (e.g., 'React Component', 'NestJS Endpoint').

componentName.description: The name of the generated component.

code.description: The code content of the generated component.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the component was generated.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the component was last updated.

definition.description: Stores user profile information.  The 'userId' parameter identifies the user.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user.

definition.description: Stores UI components and API endpoints generated by the GenAI tool, owned by the user. The structure ensures that all components are secured and only visible and editable by their owner.  Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user who owns the component.

params.name: componentId
params.description: The unique identifier for the generated component.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the WebStarter application, focusing on user-generated components. It adheres to the principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling to ensure security and scalability.  

**Authorization Independence:** The `GeneratedComponent` collection is structured under the `/users/{userId}/components/{componentId}` path, which implicitly grants ownership to the user identified by `{userId}`. No `get()` calls are required in the security rules to verify ownership, as it's derived directly from the path. This ensures atomic operations and simplifies debugging.

**Structural Segregation:** All generated components are stored within the user-specific subcollection, guaranteeing that all documents within `/users/{userId}/components` share the same security requirements (i.e., accessible only by the owning user).

**Access Modeling:** The structure utilizes path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/components/{componentId}`) which is ideal for `User 1:N GeneratedComponent` relationships. This makes security rules straightforward and efficient.

This structure allows for secure `list` operations, as the rules can simply verify that the requesting user is the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`).
